text:
Marta: quick heads up — I'm stepping offline for PTO at 20:00 UTC, need to hand off primary for the EU evening window. There's an active latency noise on generates.redwood.internal that we partially mitigated; still seeing ~300ms tail for some requests. I want a neat overlap for 30m+ for context transfer. :wave:

Dheeraj: I can shadow from 19:30 UTC and take primary at 20:00 if that works. can you paste the short runbook steps you used? also, which canary checks should I run post-handoff?

Marta: nailed it. runbook I followed is below. quick checklist I run before handing off:
- confirm incident suppression state
- snapshot `kv-cache` hit rates
- run the canary against eu-region endpoints
- confirm fallback policy is enabled (model: gptx-8q -> gptx-8q-fall)

oncall-bot: INCIDENT 24321 | HIGH — generates.redwood.internal latency spike detected. Pages were sent at 19:12 UTC. Current status: mitigated->degraded, auto-fallback enabled, suppression active for 15m after recent ACK. Links: https://incidents.redwood/24321 · Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/latency-kvcache

Dheeraj: thanks. can you paste the exact commands for the canary so I don't mangle it?

Marta: sure — two quick commands I run locally (EU cluster):
```bash
# quick kv cache health
curl -sS https://eu-metrics.redwood/internal/kvcache | jq '.hit_rate'

# canary generation (short prompt)
./scripts/canary-check.sh --region eu --model gptx-8q --count 5
```
Outputs I saw before handoff: `hit_rate` ~0.84, median latency 120ms, p99 ~ 310ms. If you see hit_rate drop below 0.6 or p99 > 500ms, escalate to L2 and consider rolling back quantization profile.

Sam: I can be secondary backup 20:00–22:00 UTC. I'll run the canary once Dheeraj flips and watch traces for errors. ping me with the snapshot link and I'll attach it to the incident. :thumbsup:

Will: FYI I queued a telemetry snapshot at 19:45 and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-ops/telemetry/24321/2026-03-03-1945.json — contains kv cache histograms and router latencies. Marta, drop that link to the incident so Dheeraj/Sam have the baseline.

Marta: added snapshot to the incident and to the runbook notes. Also left a short note on fallback thresholds in the runbook: set `fallback_threshold.p99` = 450ms to auto-route to cheaper variant.

Alex: small ask — Dheeraj, when you take over, please confirm the A/B rollout route is still pinned to the stable policy. Last week a rollout drifted and triggered ~10% user-facing regen. Steps: check `routes/api/route-weights` via `kubectl get configmap route-weights -o yaml`.

Dheeraj: got it. will do the checks in order, then post a short confirmation here (kv hit rate, canary pass, route weights) before saying "primary: handed".

Marta: perfect. also FYI I left two sticky snippets in the runbook under "quick fix": a one-liner to force KV cache reclaim and the restart order for the realtime router. Copy paste below in case you need it quickly:
```bash
# reclaim cold KV keys (use sparingly)
curl -X POST https://eu-admin.redwood/kvcache/reclaim -d '{"pct":10}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'

# graceful router restart
kubectl rollout restart deployment/realtime-router -n eu --timeout=5m
```

oncall-bot: REMINDER — scheduled primary rotation at 20:00 UTC. Please acknowledge with `ack` in thread before handoff begins.

Dheeraj: ack. starting shadowing now (19:32 UTC). running the kv hit query then canary. will report back before 20:00.

Sam: standing by, see you in the incident.

Will: watching logs, will shout if anything unexpected spikes.

Marta: thanks team — appreciated. I'll post the final handoff note right before I go offline (include contact for urgent access). :pray:
